sections.heading: Overview
sections.content:
The Single Arm Landmine Row is a unilateral back exercise performed with one end of a barbell anchored in a landmine attachment or corner.

This rowing variation allows for a unique arc of motion that targets the lats, rhomboids, and mid-back muscles effectively.

The single arm approach helps identify and correct strength imbalances between sides while also engaging the core for stabilisation.

sections.heading: Benefits
sections.content:
- Unilateral movement corrects strength imbalances between sides
- Unique arc of motion provides a different stimulus to the back muscles
- Heavy core and anti-rotation demands improve stability
- Joint-friendly movement pattern
- Allows for a greater range of motion compared to some rowing variations
- Can be loaded progressively with standard weight plates
- Builds grip strength unilaterally
- Great for developing thickness in the mid-back

sections.heading: Muscles Worked
sections.content:
Primary: Latissimus Dorsi, Rhomboids, Mid-Trapezius

Secondary: Rear Deltoids, Biceps Brachii, Core (Obliques and Transverse Abdominis), Erector Spinae, Forearms

sections.heading: Starting Position
sections.content:
1. Place one end of the barbell into a landmine apparatus or into a corner of a wall.
2. Load the free end of the barbell with the desired weight.
3. Stand facing the barbell with your feet shoulder-width apart.
4. Hinge at the hips and bend your knees slightly.
5. Grab the barbell with one hand using an overhand grip near the loaded end.
6. Keep your back straight and core engaged.
7. Let the arm hang fully extended towards the barbell.
8. Maintain a flat back with your torso at approximately 45 degrees.

sections.heading: Execution
sections.content:
1. Brace your core and maintain a straight back position.
2. Pull the barbell towards your torso, driving your elbow back.
3. Keep your elbow close to your body throughout the movement.
4. Squeeze your back muscles at the top of the row.
5. Lower the barbell back down to the starting position with control.
6. Avoid rotating your torso during the pulling motion.
7. Complete all reps on one side before switching to the other arm.
8. Breathe out as you row up, breathe in as you lower the bar.

sections.heading: Common Mistakes
sections.content:
- Rounding the lower back during the row
- Using momentum or jerking the weight up
- Excessive rotation of the torso
- Not pulling the elbow far enough back
- Standing too upright, reducing back engagement
- Gripping too far from the loaded end
- Rushing the eccentric (lowering) phase
- Shrugging the shoulder instead of retracting the scapula

sections.heading: Equipment Needed
sections.content:
- Olympic Barbell
- Landmine Attachment or Corner Setup
- Weight Plates
- Optional: Lifting Straps (for grip assistance)
- Optional: Chalk (for improved grip)

sections.heading: Landmine Setup
sections.content:
1. Secure a landmine attachment to a squat rack or heavy base.
2. Alternatively, wedge one end of the barbell into the corner of two walls or a machine.
3. Load the free end of the barbell with the desired weight plates.
4. Ensure the anchored end is stable and will not slip during the movement.
5. Test with light weight first to confirm the setup is secure.
6. Position yourself facing the free end of the barbell.

sections.heading: Body Setup
sections.content:
1. Stance: Feet shoulder-width apart, facing the barbell.
2. Hinge: Bend at the hips with knees slightly bent.
3. Grip: One hand gripping near the loaded end, overhand grip.
4. Back: Flat and neutral, approximately 45 degrees to the floor.
5. Core: Braced and tight throughout the movement.
6. Arm: Fully extended in the starting position.
7. Head: Neutral, looking slightly ahead.

sections.heading: Similar Exercises
sections.content:
- Bent Over Barbell Row: Bilateral barbell rowing movement
- Single Arm Dumbbell Row: Unilateral rowing with a dumbbell
- T-Bar Row: Similar angle with both hands
- Cable Single Arm Row: Constant tension unilateral rowing
- Meadows Row: Landmine row variation with perpendicular stance

sections.heading: Landmine Variations
sections.content:
Single Arm Landmine Row: Standard unilateral rowing movement
Double Arm Landmine Row: Both hands rowing together
Landmine Meadows Row: Perpendicular stance for greater stretch
Landmine T-Bar Row: Using a V-handle attachment for neutral grip
Landmine Bent Over Row: Traditional bent over position

sections.heading: If You Have Limitations
sections.content:
Lower Back Pain: Use a chest-supported row variation or reduce the hip hinge angle
Grip Issues: Use lifting straps or chalk for better grip
Shoulder Pain: Adjust the rowing angle or try a neutral grip
No Landmine Attachment: Wedge the barbell into a corner securely
Beginner: Start with just the bar to learn the movement pattern
Hamstring Tightness: Bend the knees more to reduce hamstring demand
